summary.data_scope: fictional constituent and payment data; simulated source feeds; offline official source

projects.title: Preserving identity and financial meaning across systems
projects.short: Reconcile constituents, engagement and contributions while retaining source keys and unmatched events.
projects.question: What is lost when a CRM migration treats source IDs and financial stages as interchangeable?
projects.architecture: Legacy/new CRM and event/donation seeds → staging → reviewed identity crosswalk → event and contribution facts → dbt tests → lifecycle mart.
decisions: Keep original source IDs while relating verified identities through a bridge.
LEFT JOIN source events to the crosswalk for reconciliation, preserving unmatched interactions.
Keep received cash, pledges and refunds as different observed financial facts.
evidence: Four fictional interactions, three matched events and one unresolved identity.
A duplicate event ID produced a dbt uniqueness-test failure; restoring the clean seed allowed the build to pass.
Two verified engaged people, one unresolved engagement, one $25 received payment, a $100 pledge and a $25 refund are present in the synthetic baseline.
projects.boundary: Prototype uses fixed fictional identities, not inferred matches or real CRM constituent data.
projects.career: CFLeads Salesforce investment/renewal logic, TLC donor reconciliation, NAACP LDF CRM integrations.

projects.title: Distinguishing missing data from missing events
projects.short: Normalize inconsistent state-style feeds and expose freshness, schema changes and retrieval history.
projects.question: If a jurisdiction returns no records, is the finding truly empty—or did ingestion fail?
projects.architecture: Simulated State A/B feeds (+ optional official Federal Register metadata) → Python normalization → validation → source-status report → analyst review.
decisions: Keep source publication time distinct from retrieval time.
Reject unexpected source-schema changes rather than silently discarding a jurisdiction.
Label simulated sources as simulated and an unfetched official source as NOT_FETCHED_OFFLINE.
evidence: An intentional State B field rename caused the normalizer to raise a ValueError.
After fixture restoration: three normalized simulated records; State A=2 and State B=1.
The official Federal Register was NOT_FETCHED_OFFLINE in the recorded offline run; a separate successful Dagster five-asset run was documented.
projects.boundary: Demonstrates source-quality handling, not comprehensive monitoring of real state legislation; the schema-failure example ran in the Python pipeline.
projects.career: NCTE cross-state legislative monitoring and CFLeads geographic engagement reporting.

projects.title: Answers that preserve approved definitions
projects.short: A deterministic question interface routes to allowlisted metrics, reports rule versions, and refuses unsupported requests.
projects.question: Can natural-language-like queries access useful analytical results without changing the rules behind them?
projects.architecture: Question → alias-based metric selection → simulated rule filtering → approved DuckDB/CSV calculation → traceable result or refusal.
decisions: The interface does not invent its own financial definitions.
Refuse unsupported causal, restricted, raw-SQL and date-filter requests.
Distinguish synthetic rule references from verified public source citations.
evidence: Recorded results: two engaged people plus one unresolved event, and a $25 receipt with a separate refund.
The source-status answer reports zero stale feeds and one official feed not fetched.
The deterministic suite recorded 20/20 checks passing, covering supported metrics and explicit refusals.
projects.boundary: Deterministic phrase router; no LLM, general RAG, true authentication, or production authorization implemented.
projects.career: CFLeads Data Wiki, investor and program metric governance, responsible AI pilot design.
